## Case

A large insurance company wants you to study the benefits of using personality assessments in their hiring policies. In the next 8 weeks you will investigate this question in several different ways.

## 1. Reliability

Before the company wants to start using personality assessment, they have asked you to make sure that the questionnaire they intend to use is reliable. The questionnaire, developed by their HR department, consists of 17 self-report items divided over 3 sub-scales (P1, P2, & P3). The questionnaire has been administered in a pilot study to 1500 people.

## 2. Sources of variation

To make sure that the information on the self-report assessment is reliable, the company also asked recruiters to judge new applications on the sub-scale P1. The idea here is that if a participant answers truthfully their answers should overlap with the judgement of the recruiter. As the insurance company works with multiple recruiting agencies, they have asked you to investigate if the recruiters are all capable judges of personality. You are given the data from 200 applicants that are each rated by 6 different judges on the items of the P1 sub-scale.
